content.comment_body: I want to enter a value into the HMI, such as 10, and have the output switch off after I pulse the input 10 times. I am unsure why it does not work—assistance needed.
Hello, your approach is quite close. Try the following suggestion:
You can manage this by configuring the memory for your variables. Check the video I attached for guidance.
Thank you for your response. I have an issue: entering 10 into an I/O field on the HMI does not work. Also, when activating V0.1, the output does not respond.
Thank you. I will try your suggestions soon because the HMI is located elsewhere. I will update you if it works.

You are referring the value to the counter's switch-off, not switch-on, which is incorrect. Additionally, your addresses are overlapping. For the HMI value, you are using VW0. VW0 includes bits from V0.0 to V1.7. If you want the bits for switching to remain on V0.1 to V0.3, assign the HMI value to a different, unused word, such as VW2.
Understood, I will assign VW2 to the tag and attempt other configurations. I'll let you know more after trying these options. Thanks for your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing trouble configuring a counter through the HMI alongside a [product_name] controller, especially with variable addressing and input field behavior. Overlapping addresses and incorrect links between HMI values and counter logic disrupt the expected operation, causing the output to not trigger as planned with user input.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to set a counter threshold value from the HMI, so that after a set number of input signals, a specific output activates.
